subject: Urgent: TempoPay reserved pool headroom squeeze — exec briefing and mitigation plan
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@tempo-pay.com>

Cc: Peter Clarke <peter.clarke@tempo-pay.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: production latency + errors this morning

Laura —

We saw a sharp increase in tail latency around 08:45 PDT and a correlated error spike (5xx rate ~4.6%) on our transactions route that uses the reserved pool. The nodes show sustained CPU/GPU busy and token queuing. Our team is throttling at the client side for now to keep downstream systems stable but this is materially impacting payments throughput.

Attached is a snapshot from our monitoring (tempo-prod-metrics-20271001.png) and we captured an elbow in throughput while concurrency held steady. Can you confirm whether Redwood is observing any reserved-capacity throttling or degraded headroom on your side?

We need a readout and ETA for mitigation. If we can’t stabilize within the hour we’ll have to trigger our incident playbook and escalate to our execs.

— Elena

Team — forwarding TempoPay’s report. Quick summary: they’re hit by a tail-latency and 5xx spike on the route backed by their reserved capacity. Customer is throttling traffic; this is customer-impacting for payments. They included metrics snapshot and expect a mitigation ETA within an hour.

Ask: Aditya — can you run a headroom and queueing check on TempoPay’s reserved pool immediately (token queue depth, GPU utilization, active batches) and confirm whether there was an autoscaler or maintenance event around 08:30–09:00 PDT?

Marissa — please prep a one-slide executive summary for Elena and copy our CSM execs; they’ve looped Peter Clarke (COO) on this thread. I’d like to avoid committing credits but we should be ready with a compensation proposal if the root cause is on our side.

I’ll hold the customer bridge if you want me to.

Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@tempo-pay.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2027 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: production latency + errors this morning — TempoPay reserved pool alert

Laura / team — initial findings:
- I see a rapid increase in queue depth on the TempoPay reserved pool starting 08:37 PDT, peaking ~08:52. Token queue depth increased ~6.2x relative to baseline for their model route.
- GPU-util on the pool is at ~98% on two nodes; observed AVX kernel hotswapping on the third node (possible transient stall during kernel selection).
- No autoscaler events or scheduled maintenance in that window. No recent model rollout for TempoPay’s pinned model.
- We are seeing significant batching latency growth (median +52 ms, p99 +420 ms) and a matched uptick in transient 5xx generated by queue timeouts in the serving runtime.

Immediate mitigations executed (10:05):
1) Increased per-tenant concurrency cap for TempoPay to allow additional inflight batches (temporary, 15 min window).
2) Enabled fallback to Quantized-XL variant for low-latency path (reduces per-request GPU time at small model-quality delta).
3) Cleared a stuck kernel on node-3 and recycled the process.

Effect: error rate reduced to ~1.3% within 12 minutes, p99 latency down ~180 ms from peak. Throughput remains ~12% below baseline due to backlog.

Next steps:
- Perform post-mortem on kernel-selection stall.
- Propose a short-term headroom bump (2 reserved GPUs for 24–72 hrs) or scheduled burst authorization while we optimize batching thresholds for their workload.

I’ll join a bridge if you spin one up.

— Aditya Rao
Director, SRE | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@tempo-pay.com>, laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TempoPay reserved pool alert — temporary customer ops plan

Elena — thank you for the flag and the metrics. We ran mitigations (Aditya’s note below) and are continuing to monitor. Quick operational notes for TempoPay ops team: 
- We recommend leaving client-side throttles in place for 30–60 minutes to let the backlog drain (avoids error flaring).
- If you need immediate throughput back to baseline, we can request a 48-hour headroom increase (2 GPUs) from infra; that requires exec approval and will be visible on next invoice unless we agree to credits.

I’m preparing the exec-level one-pager now and will include: observed impact, sequence of mitigations, customer-facing timeline, and options (headroom bump vs. quantized route + config tuning).

Elena / Peter — any preference for a short bridge now or a written summary first?

— Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: TempoPay reserved pool alert — temporary customer ops plan

Marissa / Laura — thanks for the quick response and for the temporary mitigations. The fallback to Quantized-XL is acceptable for now; quality delta is within our tolerance for payment routing. We would prefer a written summary first so we can review before pulling in our execs. If the backlog does not drain in 2 hours we will open an incident and loop COO + CEO.

Please include an estimate for the headroom bump cost and a timeline for the kernel-selection fix. We appreciate the rapid triage.

— Elena
From: david_kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@tempo-pay.com>
Date: Sun, 04 Oct 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec readout: TempoPay reserved capacity incident — summary and ask

Team / Elena — consolidated readout for TempoPay execs (one-pager attached: SLA_Reserved_Capacity_Statement.pdf):
- Impact: brief headroom exhaustion on TempoPay’s reserved pool caused elevated p99 latency and transient 5xxs between 08:37–09:10 PDT on 2027-10-02. Peak 5xx ~4.6%; error rate returned to ~1% after mitigations. Estimated lost successful transactions: ~0.8% during the window.
- Root cause (preliminary): kernel-selection stall on node-3 compounded by insufficient short-term headroom for a workload spike in concurrent short requests. No configuration changes or rollouts from customer side.
- Actions taken: cleared stuck kernel, increased per-tenant concurrency cap, enabled quantized fallback, recycled process on node-3, monitoring and backlog safe-drain.
- Proposal: authorize a 48-hour headroom increase (2 GPUs) to give breathing room while we complete a patch to the kernel-selection fallback (ETA: 72 hours). Cost estimate for headroom bump: $6,800 (net). Alternatives: prioritize a permanent configuration change to batching thresholds + pre-warming (lower ongoing cost impact).
- Ask for TempoPay: approval to provision headroom now (we can make it reversible) OR sign off on the quantized fallback as the durable short-term configuration.

Elena / Peter — Marissa will send the one-page and cost option. We’re ready to approve temporary headroom if you want us to move now. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll convert the post-mortem into an action plan with dates and owners.

— David Kim
VP, Infrastructure & Operations
Redwood Inference
